title: Contender Snap Bean: Characteristics
metaDescription: Contender snap bean is a bush snap bean variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Contender snap bean is a bush snap bean variety, also sold or known as Contender bush bean or Contender Baguio beans. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Allied Botanical (Condor brand).

heroImage.alt: Vegetable terraces and plastic tunnels on the slopes of Mankayan, Benguet, the kind of farm where Contender snap bean is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Contender bush bean or Contender Baguio beans, this is the same snap bean. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [snap bean variety finder](/crop-varieties/snap-bean), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for legumes](/land-preparation/legume-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Days to harvest, by the seller's count: first harvest 40 to 45 days after sowing. No trial on record checks this figure yet, so treat it as the seller's own and compare with farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit snap bean fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [bean fly](/pests/bean-fly), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [leafminer](/pests/leafminer), [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

Where and when to plant Contender snap bean

Baguio beans like cool weather, so most come from the highlands of Benguet and Mountain Province. Pole types bear longer, and bush types fit a short cropping gap. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Vegetables in the Philippines](/crops/vegetables-philippines).

Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.

items.q: Is Contender bush bean the same as Contender?
items.a: Yes. Contender bush bean is another name for Contender. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Contender?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
